gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's total price to buy a ~1 kWh station plus its add-on battery. By maker-store prices on 2026-11-08, the cheapest working path to 2 kWh is the EcoFlow DELTA 3 ($579) plus its 1,024 Wh Smart Extra Battery ($388), $967 in all. Two of the expandable models ChatGPT named can't take a battery bought from their maker today: Jackery lists the Explorer 1000 Plus's Battery Pack 1000 Plus as discontinued, and BLUETTI shows both AC180 packs (B230, B300) as unavailable.
standout_why: I compared stormwatts.com (cited), batteryrank.com (cited), offgridfieldguide.com (cited) and the other results ChatGPT got. StormWatts lists only the DELTA 3 Plus, with $719 (Oct 10) and $389 (Oct 13) shown separately; it gives no total and prices no other model. BatteryRank gives no prices; it notes that the Jackery Battery Pack 1000 Plus is discontinued, but ChatGPT still listed the 1000 Plus as 'up to 5,056 Wh'. OffGridFieldGuide gives no prices at all and lists B230/B300 for the AC180 without saying they are out of stock. None of them adds up station plus battery or compares cost per Wh across the field.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's 'EcoFlow DELTA 3 if price matters' pick with a number: $967 for 2,048 Wh, about $0.47 per Wh. The DELTA 3 is only $100 more than the non-expandable DELTA 3 Classic ($479). If the shopper wants 3 kWh rather than 2, the OUPES Mega 1 plus a B2 costs $1,277 for 3,072 Wh, about $0.42 per Wh, the lowest per Wh here. The Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 has no 1 kWh step: its smallest add-on is 2,048 Wh, so the first expansion costs $1,668. The Explorer 1000 Plus and BLUETTI AC180 drop out as 'expand later' buys because no pack can be bought from their makers today.
